column1: # The harness corpus.  name <TAB> spec
# `{fn}` is substituted by batch.sh with the task name cased to the target
# language's convention, exactly as in tasks.tsv.
# These are not harder algorithms. Every one of them is a few lines in every
# language the registry runs, and that is the point: the ten-task set
# saturates because its difficulty is in the implementation, so five of six
# languages score 10/10 and the instrument cannot discriminate. Difficulty
# here is in what the SUITE has to say, not in what the writer has to do.
# The one task in tasks.tsv whose expected value is a container -- `unique` --
# found three separate defects in three languages: JavaScript comparing arrays
# by reference, C# comparing List<int> by reference, and a C++ PC_CHECK macro
# that could not take an argument containing a comma. Each refused correct
# code four times. Every row below is chosen to reach a shape the assertion
# machinery has never been asked for.
# Every spec states its own edge cases and fixes any ordering, because an
# underspecified spec does not make a harder task -- it makes the tester
# invent an expectation, and then nothing downstream can say which side was
# wrong.
# a container of pairs: map/dict equality, and ordering that must not be
# left to the tester
word_count
column2: a function {fn} that takes a string of words separated by single spaces and returns each distinct word together with the number of times it occurs, ordered alphabetically by word; the empty string returns nothing; the word 'a a b' gives a twice and b once

column1: # two values from one call: tuples, out-parameters, records, pairs
min_max
column2: a function {fn} that takes a list of integers that is never empty and returns both the smallest and the largest value, smallest first; a list of one element returns that element as both

column1: # a float: an assertion that must not use exact equality
mean
column2: a function {fn} that takes a list of integers and returns their arithmetic mean as a floating point number; the empty list returns 0.0; the mean of 1 and 2 is 1.5

column1: # a container out of a string: the shape that broke three languages
parse_ints
column2: a function {fn} that takes a string of integers separated by commas and returns them in order as a list of integers; the empty string returns an empty list; the string '7' returns a list holding only 7

column1: # failure that is not a value: exceptions, error returns, options
safe_divide
column2: a function {fn} that divides its first integer argument by its second using integer division and signals an error rather than returning a number when the second is zero; 7 divided by 2 is 3

column1: # the control: if this fails, the run is about the harness or the server and
# not about any of the rows above
initials
column2: a function {fn} that takes a string of words separated by single spaces and returns the first character of each word in upper case joined together with no separator; the empty string returns the empty string
